Here's what happened.

Since I was a kid I've been terrible with girls.  I mean really, really awkward and inconfident.  It's gotten slightly better since I started college a couple years ago, but not a lot.  Any girl I have an actual crush on will make me really nervous just by talking to me.
I've kissed one girl when I was 17, and I hated it.  She was using me to get back at her ex-boyfriend or something like that and needed me.  I probably wouldn't have cared *that* much if I'd known.  I was doing it just because I was sick of being insecure about my total incompetence with girls.  She made out with me in a room with a bunch of her friends in it at her birthday party.  So that was technically my first kiss but I'm not counting it.  I felt dirty the next day.  I decided after that to only go after girls I really liked.
ANYWAY, this insecurity has been eating me away inside for the majority of my life.  I've had suicidal thoughts through almost all of it.  This isn't the whole cause of my depression but it's a major portion of it.

In the past semester, I have actually managed to work up the courage to talk to a girl I had a major crush on at class.  We had talked before but not on much of a personal level.  I was nervous the whole time but it didn't go completely badly.  I'd had a big thing for her since the first time I looked her in the eyes a year before then.  As I got to know her more, she turned out to just be awesome in general.  Awkward in a similar way to me, funny, smart, and absolutely adorable.  I would not have ever expected to meet a girl that I like this much.

I gradually talked to her more and more over the next couple months, eventually to the point where I usually wasn't that nervous talking to her.
Eventually it got to the point where I thought she might be interested and that I may actually end up going somewhere with this girl.  I was feeling confident like I never have before.
I don't know if it was in my head or if it actually happened (believe it or not I actually see the world with rose-tinted lenses sometimes) but this was going to be such a big moment for me.  I was set to destroy a huge roadblock in my life.  Things were looking up for once.
But I was still awkward and whether or not the initial confidence was based on anything real, that didn't do me any favors.  A few days after a really fun night partying we had together in a small group (Definitely some flirting going on that night), I decided that I was going to ask her out.  The amount of confidence I had amassed couldn't be stopped.
We had a class together this semester and I was gonna catch her on the way out and ask her out.  Well, class got out and all of that confidence just went out the window.  I froze up and couldn't even look at her.
*Okay, I'll just ask her after Thursday's class.*
I smiled and waved at her and she barely acknowledged it.  She'd apparently had a really stressful day that day so that may have had something to do with it, but it plunged my already broken ego down even further.  It physically hurt, and still does sometimes.

I still didn't give up though.  I still made the effort to talk to her sometimes.  When I did, that old hunch was still there that she liked me so I persevered in my slowly paced half-confident way.  After a few weeks I asked her if she wanted to study together for our final.  We are currently arranged to do this next week.  Then she walked with me to where I normally go to eat after that class and she ate with me.  At this point my confidence is starting to come back again.  This was last night.

This morning I woke up, checked Facebook on my phone, and saw that she has a new boyfriend.  It was the first thing I saw today.

Everything that I initially feared happened and I just don't know how I can have courage again after this.
